intent: Clear the last three over-cap brother_printer test modules, taking the package from fifteen violations to zero.
scope: Non-goal: no assertion changed, no test deleted, skipped or weakened
changes: test_consumables_part2.py split at TestCheckPageDelivery, which is exactly the MOD/MOD_PD boundary an earlier commit introduced. The two classes that needed MOD_PD move to test_page_delivery.py and use a plain MOD there, so the two-constant workaround dissolves rather than being carried forward: each file has one module under test again.
test_consumables.py split at TestEstimateConsumableLife: the state file and CUPS page-log tests stay, the life estimate and replacement resets go to test_consumable_estimate.py.
test_check_brother_printer.py split at TestMain: discovery and the network/USB mode selection stay, the CLI entry point and the reset flags go to test_check_brother_printer_main.py.
Renamed test_consumables_part2.py to test_counter_scales.py and narrowed its docstring, which had claimed to cover dropped-page detection that now lives in test_page_delivery.py.

verification.evidence: 402 passed - the same count as before the first of the eight commits in this package pass, so nothing was lost anywhere along the way.

verification.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest python_pkg/brother_printer/tests -q (first run after the check_brother_printer split)
verification.evidence: Reported 4 failed, 398 passed: TestResetConsumableFromPrinter travelled with TestMain and needed USBResult, which my hand-written import block had omitted. Added; the count returned to 402.
No output - python_pkg/brother_printer is entirely under the 250-line cap, down from fifteen violations at the start of the session.

verification.command: pre-commit run --files <the touched test files and artifacts>
verification.evidence: ruff, ruff format, mypy, pylint, bandit, name-tests-test and pytest-with-coverage all pass.

risks: Hand-trimmed import blocks remain the recurring risk in test splits; this pass hit it three times and the pass-count check caught it every time. A test that was already skipped would not be caught this way, but the package has none.

Several test modules are now named after the private module they cover (_page_delivery, _pjl_io, _queue_fix). If a future split renames one of those source modules, the test file names go stale even though nothing breaks.
rollback: git revert the commit; the three originals return at 275, 272 and 273 lines and the three new modules disappear.
After rollback, re-run the package suite and confirm it still reports 402 passed.
